Groups are dominated by a single galaxy, with 10 galaxies between 1 and 9 Mpc holding most of the sample's stellar mass, and a curious dearth of galaxies fainter than these dominant galaxies. Dominant halo galaxies retain gas reservoirs and ongoing star formation (extending to isolated dwarf galaxies), whereas secondary halo galaxies are often gas-depleted and quiescent. Nearly all galaxies show red giant branches indicating early-onset star formation, with one exception.
AI.conclusion: Accurate distances plus stellar masses enable a detailed characterization of the local volume: hierarchical group dominance, filament bulk flows, and a systematic dependence of gas content and star formation on a galaxy's position within its halo.

title: The slower rotation of planet-hosting stars revisited
comment: 4 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Previous studies combined rotation periods derived from Kepler photometry, stellar parameters from previous Gaia Data Releases, and planet hosts from the NASA Exoplanet Archive to conclude that statistically planet-hosting stars rotate slower than stars without detected planets. Here, we revisit these studies by using similar Kepler rotational period sample, but with an updated Gaia DR3-based stellar parameter catalogue and an updated exoplanet catalogue. We apply minimal sample cuts in evolutionary state, metallicity, and distance, and then model the stellar rotation period as a function of effective temperature alone. For each star, we derive the ratio of its observed period to the temperature-expected period, and compare the ratio distributions for the planet-host and non-host stars. For periods shorter than 20 d, the planet-host distribution of this ratio is shifted towards longer periods; the period-ratio median is ~15% larger for hosts than for non-hosts (p_KS = 2.4 x 10^-4). We also examine the recently published TESS All-Sky Rotation Survey (TARS) and find a similar trend. However, the strongly structured period distribution precludes a robust comparison between the host and the non-host stars. Therefore, the updated analysis, using more robust stellar and planetary parameters, recovers the previously reported association, strengthening the case for a genuine connection between stellar rotation and planet occurrence.

AI.tldr: Revisiting prior claims with updated Gaia DR3 stellar parameters and an updated exoplanet catalogue, the authors confirm that Kepler planet-host stars rotate ~15% slower than non-hosts for periods under 20 d, while cautioning that structured period distributions limit robustness.
AI.motivation: Earlier work linking slower stellar rotation to planet hosting relied on older Gaia data releases and out-of-date stellar and exoplanet catalogues, so the association needed re-examination with more reliable parameters.
AI.method: Uses the same Kepler rotational period sample but with a Gaia DR3-based stellar parameter catalogue and an updated exoplanet catalogue; applies minimal cuts in evolutionary state, metallicity, and distance; models rotation period as a function of effective temperature; computes each star's ratio of observed to temperature-expected period and compares ratio distributions for hosts versus non-hosts; also examines the TESS All-Sky Rotation Survey (TARS).
AI.result: For periods shorter than 20 d, the planet-host ratio distribution shifts toward longer periods, with a median ratio ~15% larger for hosts than non-hosts (p_KS = 2.4 x 10^-4). A similar trend appears in TARS, though the strongly structured period distribution prevents a robust host/non-host comparison.
AI.conclusion: The updated analysis with more robust stellar and planetary parameters recovers the previously reported association, strengthening the case for a genuine connection between stellar rotation and planet occurrence.

title: Magnetic contribution to outer-disk rotation in the spiral galaxy NGC 5055
comment: (an improved version) accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: We test whether fields of galactic strength enhance NGC~5055's outer gas rotation. Finite analytic disk decompositions yield consistent rotation--density pairs and a blended gravitational reference approximately retaining inner rotation while its density approaches the measured outer HI+He profile. This reference is modelled, not an independently measured stellar curve. Its difference from fitted gas rotation gives the required purely toroidal field for circular, axisymmetric midplane motion. The prescribed field strength at the reconstruction's inner radial boundary is $B_s$. With hydrogen inertia, no pressure and $B_s=0$, constant exponential heights of 1~kpc and 250~pc give approximate peaks of 5.47 and 10.95~$μ$G near 34.9~kpc; 0.2~kpc gives approximately 12.24~$μ$G. Extrapolated flaring exponential and Gaussian profiles peak at approximately 5.25 and 5.96~$μ$G, respectively, near 33.8~kpc. For $B_s=$8~$μ$G, their fields decline overall to approximately 5.73 and 6.30~$μ$G near 39.7~kpc. These estimates are conditional on the gravitational reference, vertical structure and prescribed boundary field. Comparison with total radio fields supports the field scale without establishing a magnetic origin for the rotation excess.

AI.tldr: The paper tests whether galactic-strength magnetic fields can account for the excess rotation in the outer gas disk of NGC 5055 by reconstructing the purely toroidal field required to support the observed rotation against a modeled gravitational reference.
AI.motivation: Outer gas rotation curves often exceed what visible matter predicts, and the authors ask whether magnetic (toroidal) field tension could supply the missing support, since galactic magnetic fields of a few μG could dynamically matter in low-density outer disks.
AI.method: Finite analytic disk decompositions give consistent rotation–density pairs and a blended gravitational reference that preserves inner rotation while matching the measured outer HI+He density profile. The difference between this reference and the fitted gas rotation yields the required purely toroidal field for circular, axisymmetric midplane motion, computed with hydrogen inertia and no pressure across several vertical thickness prescriptions (constant exponential heights, flaring exponential, Gaussian), and with a prescribed inner boundary field B_s.
AI.result: With B_s=0, constant heights of 1 kpc and 250 pc give field peaks of ~5.47 and ~10.95 μG near 34.9 kpc; 0.2 kpc gives ~12.24 μG. Flaring exponential and Gaussian profiles peak at ~5.25 and ~5.96 μG near 33.8 kpc. For B_s=8 μG, fields decline overall to ~5.73 and ~6.30 μG near 39.7 kpc.
AI.conclusion: Required field strengths are of galactic order and agree in scale with total radio field estimates, supporting the plausibility of the field magnitudes—but the estimates are conditional on the gravitational reference, vertical structure, and boundary field, and the comparison does not establish a magnetic origin for the outer rotation excess.

title: The cold substellar frontier in JWST Extragalactic surveys: a robust parallax measurement yields the most distant known ultra-cold Y dwarf
comment: 36 pages (including 9 pages of appendices), 18 figures, 11 tables, submitted to MNRAS
summary: We present an analysis of JADES-GS-BD-5, an extremely cold Y dwarf identified in the JADES/GOODS-South field. Using multi-epoch JWST/NIRCam imaging spanning a $\simeq2$-yr baseline, we calibrate the JWST astrometry and obtain the first robust parallax measurement for a brown dwarf discovered in a JWST extragalactic deep field. We measure a proper motion of $μ_{\rm tot}=49.8^{+0.3}_{-0.3}$ mas yr$^{-1}$ and a parallax of $\varpi=15.7^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ mas, corresponding to a geometric distance of $d=64^{+6}_{-5}$ pc, $\sim3\times$ further than that of the previously known most distant Y dwarfs with parallax-measured distances. We hence determine a tangential velocity of $v_{\rm tan}=15.0^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ km s$^{-1}$, consistent with a Galactic thin-disk object. We find no evidence for binary acceleration, significant photometric variability, or a plausible host. The $J$-band spectral morphology of JADES-GS-BD-5 is consistent with existing Y-dwarf templates, while its extremely faint luminosity and overall near-infrared spectral profile confirm that it is one of the coldest dwarfs discovered to date. We therefore adopt a classification of $>$Y1, consistent with a NIRCam colour-based proxy of cY1.5. The robust parallax-determined distance allows us to determine its bolometric luminosity, $\log(L_{\rm bol}/L_{\odot})=-7.08^{+0.09}_{-0.09}$. Evolutionary modelling places JADES-GS-BD-5 in the planetary-mass regime and makes it a rare benchmark for the study of cold giant-planet atmospheres. Current atmospheric models fail to reproduce its SED in detail, pointing to the importance of disequilibrium chemistry and vertical mixing. Finally, we also report additional proper motion measurements for eight of the other nine known JADES Y-dwarf candidates, highlighting JWST extragalactic surveys as a powerful route to building a statistically useful, parallax-calibrated sample of Y dwarfs.

AI.tldr: Multiepoch JWST/NIRCam imaging yields the first robust parallax for a Y dwarf found in an extragalactic deep field (JADES-GS-BD-5): d=64 pc, v_tan=15.0 km/s, log(L_bol/L_sun)=-7.08, classified as >Y1 and placing it in the planetary-mass regime.
AI.motivation: Y dwarfs are the coldest known brown dwarfs and key analogues for cold giant-planet atmospheres, but parallax-calibrated samples are sparse and limited to relatively nearby objects; JWST extragalactic deep fields offer a route to a larger, statistically useful, distance-calibrated sample.
AI.method: Analysis of JADES-GS-BD-5 using multi-epoch JWST/NIRCam imaging over a ~2-yr baseline in GOODS-South; calibration of JWST astrometry; proper-motion and parallax fitting; tests for binary acceleration, photometric variability, and a host; J-band spectral morphology comparison with Y-dwarf templates and a NIRCam colour-based spectral-type proxy; bolometric luminosity and evolutionary modelling.
AI.result: Proper motion μ_tot = 49.8±0.3 mas/yr and parallax ϖ = 15.7(+1.4/-1.3) mas, giving d = 64(+6/-5) pc (~3x farther than the most distant previously parallax-measured Y dwarfs); v_tan = 15.0(+1.4/-1.3) km/s, consistent with a thin-disk object. No binary acceleration, significant variability, or plausible host found. Spectral morphology matches Y-dwarf templates; extremely faint luminosity and NIR profile confirm it among the coldest dwarfs known; classified >Y1, consistent with colour proxy cY1.5. log(L_bol/L_sun) = -7.08±0.09; evolutionary models place it in the planetary-mass regime.
AI.conclusion: JADES-GS-BD-5 is a rare benchmark for cold giant-planet atmospheres; current atmospheric models fail to reproduce its SED in detail, indicating the importance of disequilibrium chemistry and vertical mixing. Proper motions are also reported for eight of the other nine JADES Y-dwarf candidates, demonstrating that JWST extragalactic surveys are a powerful route to a parallax-calibrated Y-dwarf sample.

title: The Milky Way-like radial structure in nearby galaxies
summary: The Milky Way exhibits a distinctive plateau in its inner surface brightness profile around one effective radius, challenging the traditional view of a purely exponential disk. To explore the origin of this feature, we identify 65 nearby galaxies ($<50$ Mpc) with similar plateau structures and analyze their multi-band surface brightness and color profiles using SDSS, DESI, 2MASS, and Mephisto data. Of the 65 galaxies with Milky Way-like plateaus, 42 have bar classifications (25 barred, 17 non-barred). Barred galaxies show radial color variations more consistent with stellar population ageing, while non-barred galaxies align more with the dust reddening direction, suggesting dust attenuation contributes to plateau formation in non-barred systems. The broad range of color gradients among barred galaxies suggests bars influence plateaus through multiple pathways, including stellar population variations and dynamical stellar-mass redistribution. Environment may also contribute: both barred and non-barred galaxies tend to reside in denser environments than a comparison sample without plateaus. The low occurrence rate ($\sim$3.6\%) may indicate that plateau structures mark a relatively uncommon evolutionary stage. The Milky Way, with both strong stellar population dependence and a persistent stellar mass profile feature, may represent an intermediate case where both stellar population variations and dynamical processes associated with the bar shape its plateau.

AI.tldr: The Milky Way's inner surface brightness plateau is investigated by identifying 65 nearby galaxies with similar plateau structures and analyzing their multi-band profiles to determine whether stellar population, dust, or dynamical (bar) effects drive the feature.
AI.motivation: The Milky Way shows a distinctive plateau in its inner surface brightness profile near one effective radius, which challenges the standard purely exponential disk picture; its physical origin is unclear.
AI.method: Selects 65 galaxies (<50 Mpc) with Milky Way-like plateaus and decomposes their multi-band surface brightness and color profiles from SDSS, DESI, 2MASS, and Mephisto data, comparing radial color variation directions against stellar-population-ageing and dust-reddening vectors, split by bar classification (25 barred, 17 non-barred) and complemented by an environmental comparison.
AI.result: Barred galaxies show color variations consistent with stellar population ageing, whereas non-barred galaxies follow dust-reddening directions, indicating dust attenuation contributes to plateau formation in non-barred systems; barred galaxies span a wide range of color gradients, implying multiple pathways including population variation and dynamical mass redistribution. Both subsets reside in denser environments than a no-plateau comparison sample, and the low occurrence rate (~3.6%) suggests plateau structures mark an uncommon evolutionary stage.
AI.conclusion: The Milky Way's plateau likely reflects an intermediate case, shaped jointly by stellar population variations and bar-related dynamical processes, consistent with its strong population dependence and persistent stellar mass profile feature.

title: First Results from JACKS: A VLA Ammonia View of Gas Heating and Star-forming Cores in the Central Molecular Zone
comment: 11 pages, 9 figures. Included in International Astronomical Union Proceedings Series: Traversing the Galactic Center in Space and Time, Proceedings IAU Symposium No. 405
summary: The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) combines warm molecular gas, strong turbulence, and a star-formation rate below that expected from its dense-gas reservoir. The JVLA Ammonia C-configuration K-band Survey (JACKS) is designed to connect these environmental conditions to the thermal and kinematic structure of compact, potentially star-forming gas. JACKS follows the footprint of the ALMA Central Molecular Zone Exploration Survey (ACES) with 31 Very Large Array mosaic fields. Its K-band setup covers the metastable NH$_3$ $(1,1)$--$(5,5)$ inversion transitions, five non-metastable NH$_3$ lines, the 22-GHz H$_2$O maser transition, H64$α$ and H66$α$, and broad continuum windows. The nominal resolutions are approximately $1.5''$ ($0.06$ pc at the Galactic Centre) and $0.4$ km s$^{-1}$ for the NH$_3$ lines. We present preliminary imaging products that demonstrate water-maser self-calibration, compact and extended continuum emission, filamentary NH$_3$ structure, and complex compact sources with multiple velocity components. Tests that combine JACKS with the SWAG and HOPS ammonia surveys recover progressively larger angular scales. These early products establish the survey's ability to connect core-scale gas heating and kinematics to the cloud-scale CMZ environment; quantitative temperature, opacity, and core-population measurements will follow from the uniformly reduced data set.

AI.tldr: JACKS is a 31-field VLA K-band mosaic survey of the CMZ following the ACES footprint, providing ~1.5'' and 0.4 km/s NH3 imaging to link environmental conditions to compact gas structure; preliminary products demonstrate water-maser self-calibration and detection of continuum, filamentary NH3, and multi-component sources.
AI.motivation: The CMZ shows warm molecular gas, strong turbulence, and a star-formation rate lower than expected from its dense-gas reservoir; JACKS aims to relate these environmental conditions to the thermal and kinematic structure of compact, potentially star-forming gas.
AI.method: A 31-field JVLA K-band mosaic matching the ACES/ALMA footprint, covering metastable NH3 (1,1)-(5,5) inversion transitions, five non-metastable NH3 lines, the 22-GHz H2O maser, H64alpha and H66alpha, and broad continuum windows, at ~1.5'' (0.06 pc) resolution and 0.4 km/s velocity resolution for NH3, with water-maser self-calibration and combination with SWAG and HOPS surveys for larger angular scales.
AI.result: Preliminary imaging yields water-maser self-calibration, compact and extended continuum emission, filamentary NH3 structure, and complex compact sources with multiple velocity components; combining with SWAG and HOPS recovers progressively larger angular scales.
AI.conclusion: Early products establish the survey's ability to connect core-scale gas heating and kinematics to the cloud-scale CMZ environment; quantitative temperature, opacity, and core-population measurements will follow from the uniformly reduced dataset.

title: Is Morphology All You Need? Quantifying Imprints of Past Star Formation in the Present-Day Morphologies of Galaxies
comment: 36 pages, 16 figures. Submitted to ApJ
summary: The next generation of galaxy surveys will bring a plethora of new observations, a vast majority of which will be observed with a few photometric broadbands, limiting the information we can infer from traditional SED fitting methods. To maximize the scientific value of these surveys, techniques that can go beyond traditional summary statistics in extracting information from galaxy observations are needed. Moving beyond integrated photometry, we introduce the Katachi-PRIME method to do spectral energy distribution (SED) based inference that jointly incorporates morphological and SED information. Katachi-PRIME uses implicit likelihood inference (ILI) to incorporate realistic morphological priors from gri broadband images, to make predictions of: stellar mass (M$_*$), specific star formation rate (sSFR), redshift (z), age (t$_{50}$), dust attenuation (Av), and gas-phase metallicity (12+log(O/H)) of the galaxy. We find that this improves constraints compared to traditional 5-band photometry. We then use the learned morphological priors to examine the extent to which morphology encodes information about past star formation, finding a stark dichotomy in how morphology encodes star formation history. While the stable morphologies of main-sequence and quiescent galaxies can predict past star formation out to $\sim 4-7$ Gyr and $\sim3-5$ Gyr, respectively, starburst and green-valley populations above and below the main sequence tend to experience structural disruptions that obscure all but the most recent star formation activity. Methods like Katachi-PRIME maximize the scientific value of future telescopes by providing broad-baseline SED-level property estimates by incorporating morphological information.

AI.tldr: Katachi-PRIME is an implicit-likelihood method that jointly uses morphology (from gri broadband images) and SED information to infer galaxy properties, improving constraints over traditional 5-band photometry and revealing a dichotomy in how morphology encodes star formation history.
AI.motivation: Next-generation galaxy surveys will mostly provide only a few photometric broadbands, limiting information obtainable from traditional SED fitting. New techniques beyond traditional summary statistics are needed to maximize scientific value by extracting more information from galaxy observations.
AI.method: Katachi-PRIME performs SED-based inference jointly incorporating morphological and SED information using implicit likelihood inference (ILI), drawing realistic morphological priors from gri broadband images. It predicts stellar mass, sSFR, redshift, age (t50), dust attenuation (Av), and gas-phase metallicity (12+log(O/H)); the learned morphological priors are then used to probe how morphology encodes past star formation.
AI.result: Joint morphology+SED inference improves constraints compared to traditional 5-band photometry. Morphology encodes star formation history with a stark dichotomy: stable main-sequence and quiescent galaxies predict past star formation out to ~4-7 Gyr and ~3-5 Gyr respectively, whereas starburst and green-valley populations experience structural disruptions obscuring all but the most recent star formation activity.
AI.conclusion: Methods like Katachi-PRIME maximize the scientific value of future telescopes by providing broad-baseline SED-level property estimates through incorporation of morphological information.

title: The Pristine survey XXXI. A stream offset from the Stream: very metal-poor stellar debris trailing 100$^{\circ}$ from the LMC-SMC system
comment: Submitted to A&A. 12 pages + 7 pages appendix (10 Figures, 3 Tables). Comments are very welcome! Note: Abstract is shortened to comply with the arXiv character limit
summary: Context: The stellar counterpart to the $200^\circ$-long HI Stream from the Clouds probes their tidally stripped stellar populations and constrains their interaction history and structure before infall into the Milky Way. Aims: We investigate the chemodynamics and possible origin of very metal-poor (VMP; [Fe/H] $<-2$) stars in the stellar Stream, targeting distant red giants selected from the Pristine--Gaia synthetic metallicity catalogue. Methods: We obtained high-resolution Gemini/GHOST spectroscopy of 33 candidate members, deriving radial velocities and metallicities. We combine these data with literature red giant members and assess their association with the Clouds using orbital integrations in a time-dependent Milky Way--LMC potential. We also compare their distribution with collisionless test particles initially placed in a diffuse LMC stellar halo. Results: We identify 12 high-confidence members based on energy and angular momentum: one intermediate metal-poor star ([Fe/H] $\sim-1.6$), ten VMP stars, and one extremely metal-poor (EMP) star ([Fe/H] $<-3$). The new VMP stars trace over $100^\circ$ of the trailing Stream, follow the Clouds' kinematics, and lie $\sim20^\circ$ from both the HI Stream and previously known, more metal-rich debris, suggesting a metallicity-dependent spatial distribution. Combined with the literature, they approximately double the known red giant sample and extend its metallicity range from [Fe/H] $\sim-0.5$ to $-4.3$. Orbital integrations support an association with the Clouds, while test particles reproduce the debris' broad spatial distribution. Conclusions: VMP and EMP stars contribute to the Clouds' tidal debris. They may originate in the extended stellar halos of the LMC or SMC, or in disrupted satellites. Their spatial and kinematic properties can constrain future simulations of the Milky Way--LMC--SMC interaction.

AI.tldr: High-resolution Gemini/GHOST spectroscopy of 33 candidate red giants reveals 12 high-confidence members (ten very metal-poor, one extremely metal-poor) of the ~200° stellar Stream trailing the Magellanic Clouds, which follow Cloud kinematics, trace >100° of the Stream, and double the known red giant sample to [Fe/H] ~ -4.3, with orbital integrations supporting a Magellanic association.
AI.motivation: The stellar counterpart to the 200°-long HI Stream offers a probe of the Clouds' tidally stripped stellar populations and can constrain their interaction history and structure prior to Milky Way infall; specifically, the origin and chemodynamics of very metal-poor stars in the Stream remain poorly characterized.
AI.method: Targeted distant red giants selected from the Pristine–Gaia synthetic metallicity catalogue; high-resolution Gemini/GHOST spectroscopy of 33 candidates to derive radial velocities and metallicities; membership assessed via energy and angular momentum; association with the Clouds tested with orbital integrations in a time-dependent MW–LMC potential; spatial distribution compared against collisionless test particles placed in a diffuse LMC stellar halo.
AI.result: 12 high-confidence members identified: one intermediate metal-poor ([Fe/H] ~ -1.6), ten VMP, one EMP ([Fe/H] < -3). New VMP stars trace >100° of the trailing Stream, follow the Clouds' kinematics, and lie ~20° from the HI Stream and known metal-richer debris, indicating a metallicity-dependent spatial distribution. Combined with literature, the red giant sample is roughly doubled and its metallicity range extended from [Fe/H] ~ -0.5 to -4.3. Orbital integrations support a Cloud association; test particles reproduce the broad spatial distribution of the debris.
AI.conclusion: VMP and EMP stars contribute to the Clouds' tidal debris, potentially originating in the extended stellar halos of the LMC or SMC or in disrupted satellites. Their spatial and kinematic properties provide constraints for future simulations of the MW–LMC–SMC interaction.

title: A Large-Sample Study of Interstellar Reddening in Galactic Star Clusters
comment: 11 pages, 9 figures, 1 table, submitted to A&A
summary: The interstellar reddening (extinction or absorption) is caused mainly by the dust grains of different sizes and compounds. All astrophysical observations are somehow affected by this effect, depending on the wavelength and location of the observed object. Different methods and techniques have been developed over the last nearly one hundred years to determine the reddening and to map the solar neighbourhood. The members of open clusters are a consistent population of stars formed together with a homogeneous metallicity. Therefore, the reddening can be estimated in a statistical way, avoiding all problems of single stars and spectral-energy-distribution fitting, for example. Other than for most available works, we can also use more massive upper main-sequence stars for the analysis. We used classical colour-colour diagrams (also known as the Q-method) for (B-V), (BP-RP), (U-B), (U-BP), (U-RP), and (U-G) to determine consistent mean reddening values and their errors. The corresponding standard lines for the fitting are independent of the age and metallicity. We determined colour excesses for 5377 Galactic open clusters covering Galactocentric distances from two to twenty kpc, respectively. The derived values were checked with existing dust and extinction maps. In general, we found good agreement. The solar neighbourhood of +-1500 pc shows a very patchy structure of the dust composition. Our results lay the foundations for constructing a new map of the reddening (dust) distribution and estimating clusters' metallicities by isochrone fitting, keeping the distances and reddening values fixed.

AI.tldr: The authors determine consistent mean interstellar reddening values and errors for 5377 Galactic open clusters spanning Galactocentric distances of 2–20 kpc, using the classical Q-method (colour-colour diagrams) applied to upper main-sequence stars with age- and metallicity-independent standard lines.
AI.motivation: Interstellar reddening caused by dust grains affects all astrophysical observations depending on wavelength and location, motivating a robust, statistical determination of reddening and mapping of the solar neighbourhood. Open clusters offer a homogeneous stellar population that avoids the problems of single-star and spectral-energy-distribution fitting, and permits use of massive upper main-sequence stars, unlike most existing works.
AI.method: Classical colour-colour (Q-method) diagrams were constructed for six colour combinations: (B-V), (BP-RP), (U-B), (U-BP), (U-RP), and (U-G). Standard fitting lines independent of age and metallicity were used to derive mean reddening values and errors in a statistical manner across the cluster sample.
AI.result: Colour excesses were obtained for 5377 Galactic open clusters over Galactocentric distances from 2 to 20 kpc. The derived values were cross-checked against existing dust and extinction maps, showing general good agreement. The solar neighbourhood within ±1500 pc exhibits a very patchy dust-composition structure.
AI.conclusion: The results provide a foundation for constructing a new reddening (dust) distribution map and for estimating cluster metallicities via isochrone fitting with distances and reddening values held fixed.

title: Constraining the timescale of activity in Mrk 1018
comment: Submitted to PASA
summary: We present analysis of an extended emission line region projected 3.77 kpc from the nucleus of the canonical changing-look AGN Mrk~1018, found in MUSE integral-field observations from the Close AGN Reference Survey. Emission-line ratios show that the region exhibits AGN ionisation but has a very low velocity dispersion, $77 \pm 1$ kms$^{-1}$, ruling out an ionised outflow. The lower limit on the light travel time is $12{,}300 \pm 2{,}300$ yr, implying that the nucleus has therefore been active for at least this long. This is much longer than the duration of either observed changing-look transition, which occurred over several years. This implies that Mrk 1018's multi-year variations are occurring within a longer term active phase.

AI.tldr: A luminous extended emission-line region 3.77 kpc from the nucleus of the changing-look AGN Mrk 1018 shows AGN-like ionization but low velocity dispersion, indicating the nucleus has been active for at least ~12,300 yr—far longer than its multi-year changing-look transitions.
AI.motivation: Changing-look AGN (CLAGN) Mrk 1018 exhibits dramatic, multi-year transitions in broad-line visibility, raising the question of whether these variations reflect a genuinely brief nuclear active phase or shorter-term fluctuations within a more sustained period of accretion activity.
AI.method: Analysis of an extended emission-line region (EELR) projected 3.77 kpc from the nucleus using MUSE integral-field spectroscopy from the Close AGN Reference Survey (CARS); emission-line ratio diagnostics and velocity dispersion measurements are used to characterize the ionization source and kinematics, and the projected radius yields a lower limit on the light-travel time.
AI.result: Emission-line ratios indicate AGN ionization, while the low velocity dispersion of 77 ± 1 km/s rules out an ionized outflow (i.e., the gas is photoionized in situ rather than outflowing). The projected separation gives a light-travel-time lower limit of 12,300 ± 2,300 yr, implying nuclear activity for at least this duration—much longer than the several-year timescales of the observed changing-look transitions.
AI.conclusion: Mrk 1018 has hosted an active nucleus for at least ~12,000 yr, so its dramatic multi-year changing-look variability occurs within a longer-term active phase rather than representing the onset or termination of an accretion episode; the EELR provides an independent archaeological record of past AGN luminosity.

title: Violent relaxation in hierarchical stellar systems: pathways toward massive black hole formation in the early Universe
comment: 17 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, submitted to A&A
summary: Massive stellar systems have been detected in the high-redshift Universe via the James Webb Space Telescope using gravitational lensing techniques. Such stellar systems may evolve on short dynamical timescales, despite a formally large 2-body relaxation time. If the stellar system consists of a large number of gravitationally bound clusters, a 2-body relaxation time can be defined for the star clusters in analogy to the 2-body relaxation time for stars, implying a faster evolution determined by the number of stars per cluster. At their formation, clusters will go through a process of "cold collapse" as part of their early, non-collisional, evolution. This phase enhances the mass segregation between the more massive and less massive population of stars. We derive a criteria based on the mass of the two components that determines under which conditions the massive component may even decouple from the cluster itself. Mergers of clusters and multiple mergers on average tend to produce systems with larger cluster radii. For the formation of massive black holes via dense stellar systems, the most promising pathway consists in the cold collapse of a dense massive cluster, after few mergers (or possibly none). In such a cluster with a sufficient number of massive stars, the massive population of stars will dynamically decouple in the central region and go through core collapse, leading to the formation of a central massive object. In the case of multiple mergers, massive but more spatially extended stellar systems will form.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that gravitational-lensing-detected massive high-z stellar systems can evolve on short dynamical timescales if they consist of many bound clusters, since the cluster-level 2-body relaxation time scales with the small number of stars per cluster; cold collapse and mergers then drive mass segregation and can lead to central massive black hole formation.
AI.motivation: JWST has discovered massive stellar systems at high redshift through gravitational lensing, and their apparent short dynamical evolution times conflict with a formally long stellar 2-body relaxation time. The authors seek a framework that reconciles this apparent inconsistency and clarifies how such systems can form massive central objects.
AI.method: The authors define an analogous 2-body relaxation time for star clusters treated as gravitationally bound "particles," which depends on the number of stars per cluster rather than the total number of stars. They analyze the early non-collisional "cold collapse" phase, derive a criterion based on the masses of the massive and less massive stellar components to determine when the massive component dynamically decouples, and assess the effect of cluster mergers (single and multiple) on cluster radii.
AI.result: Cold collapse enhances mass segregation between massive and less massive stars, and a mass-ratio criterion identifies conditions under which the massive component decouples from the cluster. Mergers, and especially multiple mergers, on average produce systems with larger cluster radii, yielding massive but spatially extended stellar systems.
AI.conclusion: The most promising pathway to massive black hole formation in dense stellar systems is cold collapse of a dense massive cluster after few or no mergers: with sufficient massive stars, the massive population decouples in the central region, undergoes core collapse, and forms a central massive object. Multiple mergers instead yield massive but more extended systems, disfavoring such formation.

title: Multi-layer magnetic structure toward NGC 1333 revealed by a square-degree optical polarimetric survey
comment: 19 pages, 17 figures, accepted by A&A
summary:
Magnetic-field studies of star-forming regions are complicated by overlapping structures along the line of sight. We investigate the large-scale magnetic field toward NGC~1333 in Perseus, accounting for foreground polarization through stellar distances and optical polarimetry.
  Our wide-field $R$-band survey covers nearly one square degree and provides polarization measurements for approximately 840 stars, with distances from Gaia DR3 and StarHorse. We used polarization-distance trends and Stokes parameters to identify line-of-sight components and estimate foreground polarization. After subtracting it in Stokes space, we characterized the field using circular statistics and the angular dispersion function (ADF), comparing it with molecular-line and complementary polarimetric observations.
  The data reveal a polarized foreground at 160-300 pc and a cloud component beyond 300 pc. After correction, the plane-of-sky field rotates smoothly from $126.3°\pm0.8°$ in the northwest to $162.2°\pm0.6°$ in the southeast, remaining well ordered in both regions. The ADF gives turbulent-to-ordered field ratios of $0.054^{+0.025}_{-0.022}$ and $0.095^{+0.021}_{-0.047}$, corresponding to plane-of-sky strengths of $59^{+44}_{-23}$ and $46^{+50}_{-13}~μ\mathrm{G}$. Residual foreground fluctuations may affect these estimates. CO data show multiple velocity components with spatially varying contributions. Corrected optical polarization agrees with the large-scale orientation traced by Planck, while near-infrared and JCMT/POL-2 data reveal localized deviations in denser structures.
  Our results indicate a coherent cloud-scale magnetic field with a smoothly changing orientation, alongside localized variations in dense structures. They demonstrate the value of combining stellar distances and wide-field optical polarimetry to disentangle foreground contributions.

AI.tldr: A wide-field R-band optical polarimetric survey of ~840 stars toward NGC 1333 (Perseus), combined with Gaia DR3/StarHorse distances, disentangles foreground polarization and reveals a coherent, smoothly rotating cloud-scale magnetic field.
AI.motivation: Magnetic-field studies of star-forming regions are confounded by overlapping structures along the line of sight; foreground polarization must be separated to recover the cloud's intrinsic field.
AI.method: Nearly one square degree R-band survey yielding polarization for ~840 stars with Gaia DR3/StarHorse distances. Polarization-distance trends and Stokes parameters identify line-of-sight components and estimate foreground polarization; after Stokes-space subtraction, the field is characterized via circular statistics and the angular dispersion function (ADF), compared with molecular-line and complementary polarimetric data (Planck, NIR, JCMT/POL-2).
AI.result: A polarized foreground at 160-300 pc and a cloud component beyond 300 pc are found. Corrected plane-of-sky field rotates from 126.3°±0.8° (NW) to 162.2°±0.6° (SE), remaining well ordered. ADF gives turbulent-to-ordered ratios of 0.054(+0.025/-0.022) and 0.095(+0.021/-0.047), implying plane-of-sky strengths of 59(+44/-23) and 46(+50/-13) μG. CO shows multiple velocity components; corrected optical polarization agrees with Planck large-scale orientation, while NIR and JCMT/POL-2 show localized deviations in denser structures.
AI.conclusion: NGC 1333 hosts a coherent cloud-scale magnetic field with smoothly changing orientation plus localized variations in dense structures. Combining stellar distances with wide-field optical polarimetry is valuable for disentangling foreground contributions, though residual foreground fluctuations may bias field-strength estimates.

title: Octavius: A High-Performance Analysis Toolkit for Galaxy Simulations
comment: 17 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to RAS Techniques and Instruments. Code is available at https://github.com/jp-duminy/octavius ; documentation is hosted at https://octavius.readthedocs.io
summary: Increased computing power and more efficient codes have allowed cosmological simulations of galaxy formation to grow massively in scale: the analysis of their outputs has consequently become a big data computational challenge. We present Octavius, a high-performance, hybrid-parallel simulation analysis toolkit. Octavius ingests a simulation snapshot with associated halo catalogue, locates galaxies with a 6D friends-of-friends algorithm, then produces an HDF5 catalogue of properties for haloes, subhaloes, and galaxies. The analysis is fast and memory efficient: we compare the performance against the widely used predecessor toolkit, Caesar, and show Octavius delivers order-of-magnitude improvements in speed with a factor of >5 reduction in peak memory. We demonstrate near-linear strong scaling of compute and linear peak memory scaling with the number of halo-assigned particles. Compute times scale with the superlinear computational load of larger haloes; we note the pipeline is presently I/O-limited. The code is written in Python and uses a declarative, plugin-based architecture so as to be easily extensible. Octavius can currently analyse SIMBA, SWIFT-KIARA, SWIFT-EAGLE, SWIFT-COLIBRE, and TNG snapshots; AHF, HBT-HERONS, and SUBFIND halo catalogues are supported. Properties computed include masses, galaxy photometry with dust attenuation, and kinematic, radial, morphological, and virial quantities. Output catalogues are easily accessed through a provided user API. The code is open sourced at https://github.com/jp-duminy/octavius

AI.tldr: Octavius is a high-performance, hybrid-parallel, Python-based simulation analysis toolkit that ingests snapshots plus halo catalogues, finds galaxies via a 6D friends-of-friends algorithm, and outputs HDF5 catalogues of halo, subhalo, and galaxy properties, achieving order-of-magnitude speedups and >5x lower peak memory than Caesar.
AI.motivation: Cosmological galaxy formation simulations have grown massively in scale due to increased computing power and more efficient codes, making analysis of simulation outputs a big data computational challenge. Existing toolkits such as Caesar are too slow and memory-hungry for this scale.
AI.method: Octavius ingests a simulation snapshot with its associated halo catalogue, locates galaxies using a 6D friends-of-friends algorithm, and produces an HDF5 catalogue of halo, subhalo, and galaxy properties. It is written in Python with a declarative, plugin-based architecture for extensibility, and uses hybrid parallelism. Performance is benchmarked against Caesar, with strong-scaling and memory-scaling tests. Supported inputs include SIMBA, SWIFT-KIARA, SWIFT-EAGLE, SWIFT-COLIBRE, and TNG snapshots, with AHF, HBT-HERONS, and SUBFIND halo catalogues. Computed properties include masses, dust-attenuated photometry, and kinematic, radial, morphological, and virial quantities, accessible via a user API.
AI.result: Octavius achieves order-of-magnitude speed improvements and more than 5x reduction in peak memory versus Caesar. It shows near-linear strong scaling in compute and linear peak-memory scaling with the number of halo-assigned particles. Compute times scale with the superlinear computational load of larger haloes, and the pipeline is currently I/O-limited.
AI.conclusion: Octavius is a fast, memory-efficient, scalable, and extensible toolkit that addresses the big data challenge of cosmological simulation analysis, is broadly compatible with major simulation and halo-finder outputs, and is open-sourced on GitHub.

title: G92.4+5.0: A Perseus Arm superbubble associated with the H II region CTB 102
comment: Submitted to the Astrophysical Journal; comments welcome
summary: Superbubbles are vast hot cavities carved out by the stellar winds and supernovae of clusters of high-mass stars. We investigate G92.4+5.0 (the CTB 102 superbubble), a Perseus Arm superbubble associated with the HII region CTB 102. We use new and archival radio observations (total intensity, rotation measure, and HI spectral line) from the Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory Synthesis Telescope, combined with single-antenna data from the Effelsberg Medium Latitude Survey, the Global Magneto-Ionic Medium Survey, and the HI4PI survey to provide data on large structures. The upper region of the superbubble is faint in HI. In order to detect its full extent, we supplement our observations with H-alpha data from the Wisconsin H-Alpha Mapper Survey and the Ziegenbalg Survey, and observe H-alpha emission in the upper region. We measure the CTB 102 superbubble to be at least ~170 pc wide and ~420 pc tall, with an expansion rate of ~12 km/s in the lower regions of the superbubble and ~22.5 km/s in the upper regions. The elongated structure and increasing expansion rate with height are consistent with the evolutionary properties of a superbubble described by the Kompaneets model. We fit the Kompaneets model to the CTB 102 superbubble and obtain an estimated age of 1-6 Myr. This supports a possible scenario in which the stellar cluster currently ionizing CTB 102 is the expansion energy source for the superbubble. Alternatively, if the superbubble expanded under the power of a previous generation of stars, the current CTB 102 stellar cluster may have formed in the walls of the superbubble.

AI.tldr: Multi-wavelength study of the CTB 102 superbubble (G92.4+5.0) in the Perseus Arm, measuring it at least ~170 pc wide and ~420 pc tall with expansion rates of ~12 km/s (lower) and ~22.5 km/s (upper), consistent with a Kompaneets model yielding an age of 1-6 Myr.
AI.motivation: Superbubbles are vast hot cavities carved by stellar winds and supernovae of high-mass stellar clusters; the authors aim to characterize the structure, kinematics, and evolutionary state of the poorly studied CTB 102 superbubble associated with the HII region CTB 102.
AI.method: New and archival radio observations (total intensity, rotation measure, HI spectral line) from the DRAO Synthesis Telescope, combined with single-antenna data from the Effelsberg Medium Latitude Survey, the Global Magneto-Ionic Medium Survey, and HI4PI for large-scale structure. Because the upper region is HI-faint, H-alpha data from the Wisconsin H-Alpha Mapper Survey and the Ziegenbalg Survey were added to trace the full extent. Expansion kinematics were then fit with the Kompaneets model.
AI.result: The superbubble measures at least ~170 pc wide and ~420 pc tall, with an expansion rate of ~12 km/s in the lower regions and ~22.5 km/s in the upper regions. The elongated morphology and increasing expansion velocity with height match Kompaneets-model evolutionary predictions, giving an estimated age of 1-6 Myr.
AI.conclusion: The Kompaneets fit supports a scenario in which the stellar cluster currently ionizing CTB 102 is the expansion energy source; alternatively, if the bubble expanded under a previous stellar generation, the current CTB 102 cluster may have formed in the superbubble walls.

title: Rotational Excitation of HC$_5$NH$^+$ by He: Collision Dynamics and Astrophysical Applications
comment: 7 pages, 7 figures
summary: Reliable collisional rate coefficients are crucial for interpreting the rotational emission spectra of molecules in interstellar clouds. In this work, we construct a two-dimensional potential energy surface (PES) for the $\mathrm{HC}_5\mathrm{NH}^+$--He system at the CCSD(T)-F12B/cc-pVTZ-F12 level of theory. Rotationally inelastic cross sections are calculated using the quantum close-coupling (CC) method, and the corresponding collisional rate coefficients are obtained by thermal averaging over a Maxwell--Boltzmann distribution. We use these collisional data in a non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (non-LTE) radiative transfer model to investigate the excitation of $\mathrm{HC}_5\mathrm{NH}^+$ in the cold dark cloud TMC-1. A global $χ^2$ minimization analysis of seven observed lines yields best-fitting values of $n(\mathrm{H}_2)=1.63\times10^{5}$\,cm$^{-3}$ and $N(\mathrm{H}_2)=5.09\times10^{11}$\,cm$^{-2}$, with reduced $χ^2_{\min}=0.87$. The modelled line intensities are in good agreement with the observations. These results provide insight into the collisional excitation and radiative properties of $\mathrm{HC}_5\mathrm{NH}^+$ under the physical conditions prevailing in TMC-1.

AI.tldr: This work computes a CCSD(T)-F12B/cc-pVTZ-F12 potential energy surface and quantum close-coupling collisional rate coefficients for HC5NH+--He, then applies them in a non-LTE radiative transfer model to constrain the excitation and physical conditions of HC5NH+ in TMC-1.
AI.motivation: Reliable collisional rate coefficients are essential for interpreting rotational emission spectra of interstellar molecules; such data for HC5NH+ were lacking, limiting accurate non-LTE modeling of its excitation in cold clouds.
AI.method: A two-dimensional PES for the HC5NH+--He system was built at the CCSD(T)-F12B/cc-pVTZ-F12 level. Rotationally inelastic cross sections were obtained via the quantum close-coupling (CC) method, and rate coefficients were derived by thermal averaging over a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution. These collisional data were incorporated into a non-LTE radiative transfer model to analyze HC5NH+ excitation in TMC-1.
AI.result: Global chi-squared minimization over seven observed lines gives best-fit n(H2)=1.63e5 cm^-3 and N(H2)=5.09e11 cm^-2 with reduced chi^2_min=0.87; modeled line intensities agree well with observations.
AI.conclusion: The derived collisional and radiative data provide insight into the excitation properties of HC5NH+ under the physical conditions of TMC-1 and support reliable non-LTE modeling of its observed emission.

title: SDSS-V LVM: Spatial Resolution Effects on Diagnostic Diagrams in the Magellanic Clouds
comment: 20 pages, 9 figures
summary: We investigate how spatial resolution affects emission-line diagnostics in the interstellar medium (ISM) of the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds (SMC and LMC) using SDSS Local Volume Mapper (LVM) data obtained at and degraded to 19, 42, 170 pc (for the SMC) and 17, 68, 272 pc (for the LMC), respectively. We compare the distributions of strong emission-line ratios through 1D and 2D Kolmogorov Smirnov tests. We deduced that diagnostics involving ionization and density sensitive ratios such as [OIII]λ5007/H\b{eta}, [SII]λλ6717+6731/Hα and [NII]λ6584/Hα are the most strongly impacted by resolution loss in this order. The SMC shows significant deviations even from intermediate scales (42 pc), whereas for the LMC, the coarsest resolution (272 pc) remains relatively stable, indicating that the SMC is intrinsically more affected by spatial mixing. Resolution degradation produces a marked homogenization effect: extreme values present at the finest scales are progressively diluted, causing diagnostic diagrams to converge toward their mean loci. Diffuse ionized gas is particularly sensitive to this mixing, while Hα selected ionized regions exhibit more robust behavior across resolutions. The sensitivity of diagnostic diagrams involving emission-line ratios, equivalent widths, and kinematic properties varies with both spatial resolution and galaxy, with the SMC generally showing stronger changes than the LMC. Our results demonstrate that sub-50 pc resolution is required to resolve the detailed structure of low-metallicity galaxies, and they highlight at least the need for careful interpretation of line-ratio diagnostics in extragalactic studies where coarse spatial resolution is unavoidable.

AI.tldr: Spatial resolution degradation in LVM data of the SMC and LMC systematically homogenizes ISM emission-line ratios, biasing diagnostics most strongly for ionization- and density-sensitive ratios; sub-50 pc resolution is needed to resolve low-metallicity galaxy structure.
AI.motivation: Extragalactic emission-line diagnostics are commonly applied at spatial resolutions far coarser than the physical scales of ISM structure, yet the quantitative impact of resolution loss on the resulting line-ratio distributions and diagnostic diagrams is poorly characterized.
AI.method: Using SDSS Local Volume Mapper integral-field data of the SMC and LMC, the authors degraded spatial sampling to 19/42/170 pc (SMC) and 17/68/272 pc (LMC) and compared strong emission-line ratio distributions via 1D and 2D Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests, also assessing equivalent widths and kinematic properties across resolutions.
AI.result: Diagnostics using [OIII]λ5007/Hβ, [SII]λλ6717+6731/Hα, and [NII]λ6584/Hα are most strongly affected, in that order. The SMC shows significant deviations already at 42 pc, while the LMC stays relatively stable even at 272 pc, indicating the SMC is intrinsically more susceptible to spatial mixing. Degradation dilutes extreme values, driving diagnostic diagrams toward their mean loci; diffuse ionized gas is especially resolution-sensitive, whereas Hα-selected ionized regions are more robust.
AI.conclusion: Resolution loss produces a homogenization effect that varies with both spatial scale and galaxy (SMC more than LMC). Sub-50 pc resolution is required to resolve detailed structure in low-metallicity galaxies, and coarse-resolution extragalactic line-ratio diagnostics must be interpreted with caution.
